speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you've mentioned episodes of unresponsiveness accompanied by facial grimacing; can you tell me exactly what happens during these episodes and how long they last?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Complex Partial Seizure (Temporal Lobe Epilepsy)

The patient's age, specific semiology (facial grimacing, hand gestures, automatism), ictal taste disturbance (dysgeusia), and post-ictal confusion are highly characteristic of a temporal lobe seizure. I will proceed with ordering diagnostic tests to confirm this.
REQUEST TEST: EEG (Electroencephalogram)
REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Brain
